svg.text: Veroboard (stripboard) layout: Adafruit ADS1115 (STEMMA QT) upside down on sockets, six track cuts

Component side, copper strips shown through the board. 17 strips × 26 holes (about 66 × 43 mm). The module plugs into two 6-way sockets chip side down, so its pins are mirrored, and lifts out. Checked against the schematic before drawing.
bench: a wire to any free hole on strip 7
car: tank bond strap to chassis
col 13, strips 9–14: A+ A3 A2 A1 A0 A−
col 18, strips 9–14: VIN GND SCL SDA ADDR ALRT
col 26: strip 15 ground sense, strip 16 sender
Module: upside down, chip towards the board, so its pins
are mirrored: analogue row (A+ … A−) in the left socket,
I²C row (VIN … ALRT) in the right, A+ and VIN on strip 9.
Nothing sits under the module: its parts face the board.
The 6 cuts give strips 9–14 an analogue half and an I²C half.
Capacitors return to A− (the ADC's own ground).
ADDR, ALRT, A+ and A2: nothing else on their half-strips.
Do not bridge the address jumper (module's back, now on top).
Strips 3, 4, 5 and 8 belong to the display: keep clear.
Taps beyond each load: 3.3 V enters strip 17 at col 24,
so R1 (col 1) is past Rp (col 22); R2 and R3 are past
Rp and R4 as seen from J2 (col 26).
Sender: ① signal to J2 strip 16, ③ sense to the sender
body, ② body to GND. Without ③ the gauge shows GROUND FAULT.
Before plugging in the display or the module
1. Check each cut with a meter: no continuity between the left and right halves of strips 9–14.
2. Unpowered: no continuity between strips except the linked groups 6–9R–17 (3.3 V), 7–10R (GND), 1–11R (SCL), 2–12R (SDA), where R is the right-hand half.
3. Offer the board up to the case: strip 1 must meet the socket labelled 18, strip 8 the socket labelled 5V.
4. Display only, no module: strip 6 ≈ 3.3 V, strip 8 ≈ 5 V. Then fit the module chip side down (A+ top left, VIN top right) and power up.
J1: male header into the display's sockets; clip or screw the board to the case so it cannot work loose. J2: latching 2.54 mm connector (for example Molex KK 254).
J3 (dashed): optional, to feed the display from an external 5 V supply through its 5V socket. Check the board's power path first (WIRING.md), and never connect USB at the same time.
